source_text: Τὸ δὲ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα οὐ παραιτεῖται ἡ Γραφὴ καλεῖν ἀγαθὸν, κατὰ τὸν Δαβὶδ τὸν λέγοντα· Τὸ Πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἀγαθὸν ὁδηγήσει με ἐν γῇ εὐθείᾳ. Καὶ ὅτε πάλιν ὁ Κύριος λέγει περὶ ἑαυτοῦ· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ζῶν, ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς. Ἀλλαχοῦ τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα καλεῖ ἄρτον οὐράνιον λέγων· Τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον. Ἐδίδαξε γὰρ ἡμᾶς ἐν τῇ εὐχῇ ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι αἰτεῖν τὸν ἐπιούσιον ἄρτον, τουτέστι τὸν μέλλοντα, οὗ ἀπαρχὴν ἔχομεν ἐν τῇ νῦν ζωῇ, τῆς σαρκὸς τοῦ Κυρίου μεταλαμβάνοντες, καθὼς αὐτὸς εἶπεν· Ὁ ἄρτος δὲ, ὃν ἐγὼ δώσω, ἡ σάρξ μου ἐστὶν ὑπὲρ τῆς τοῦ κόσμου ζωῆς. Πνεῦμα γὰρ ζωοποιοῦν ἡ σάρξ ἐστι τοῦ Κυρίου, διότι ἐκ Πνεύματος τοῦ ζωοποιοῦ συνελήφθη. Τὸ γὰρ γεγεννημένον ἐκ τοῦ Πνεύματος Πνεῦμά ἐστι. Καὶ ὅτε λέγει ὁ Ἱερεμίας περὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὅτι αὐτὸς ὡδήγησε τὸν Ἰσραὴλ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Καὶ οὐκ εἴπατε, φησὶ, Ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ Κύριος, ὁ ἀναγαγὼν ἡμᾶς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου, ὁ καθοδηγήσας ἡμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ; Ὁ Ἡσαΐας τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον εἶπεν ὡδηγηκέναι τὸν Ἰσραὴλ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· ἔστι γοῦν ἀκοῦσαι αὐτοῦ λέγοντος· Ἤγαγεν αὐτοὺς διὰ τῆς 1013 ἀβύσσου ὡς ἵππον διὰ τῆς ἐρήμου· καὶ οὐκ ἐκοπίασαν, καὶ ὡς κτήνη διὰ τοῦ πεδίου. Καὶ κατέβη Πνεῦμα παρὰ Κυρίου, καὶ ὡδήγησεν αὐτούς. Πρὸς δὲ Κορινθίους γράφει ὁ Ἀπόστολος, ὅτι Χριστὸς ἦν ὁ ὁδηγῶν· Ἔπινον γὰρ ἐκ πνευματικῆς ἀκολουθούσης πέτρας· ἡ δὲ πέτρα ἦν ὁ Χριστός. Καὶ ὅτε λέγει ὁ Παῦλος ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ κεκλῆσθαι αὐτόν· Ὁ Θεὸς, φησὶν, ὁ ἀφορίσας με ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός μου, καὶ καλέσας διὰ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, ἀποκαλύψαι τὸν Υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ, ἵνα εὐαγγελίζωμαι αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι. Ῥωμαίους δὲ ὑπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ κεκλῆσθαι λέγει γράφων πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐν οἷς ἐστε καὶ ὑμεῖς κλητοὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Τὸ δὲ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸν Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Βαρνάβαν κεκληκέναι εἴρηκεν εἰς τὸ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εὐαγγελίσασθαι τὸν Χριστόν. Καὶ τό γε θαυμαστὸν, τοῦ Ἰησοῦ εἰπόντος Παύλῳ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ· Πορεύου, ὅτι εἰς ἔθνη μακρὰν ἐξαποστέλλω σε· καὶ τοῦ Παύλου Γαλάταις γράφοντος, Παῦλος ἀπόστολος οὐκ ἀπ' ἀνθρώπων, οὐδὲ δι' ἀνθρώπου, ἀλλὰ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς τοῦ ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν· καὶ μετ' ὀλίγον· Γνωρίζω δὲ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοὶ, τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον τοῦτο, ὅτι οὐκ ἔστι κατὰ ἄνθρωπον· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐγὼ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου παρέλαβον αὐτὸ, οὐδὲ ἐδιδάχθην, ἀλλὰ δι' ἀποκαλύψεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἀποστεῖλαν τόν τε Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Βαρνάβαν φαίνεται, κηρῦξαι τοῖς ἔθνεσι τὸν Χριστόν. Καὶ ὁτὲ μὲν ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ Πατρὸς λαλοῦσιν οἱ προφῆται, ὡς ὅταν ἐν Ψαλμοῖς λέγῃ ὁ Θεός· Ἅπαξ ὤμοσα ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ μου, Εἰ τῷ Δαβὶδ ψεύσομαι, τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα μενεῖ, καὶ ὁ θρόνος αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐναντίον μου· καὶ πάλιν· Ἐκ καρποῦ τῆς ὀσφύος σου θήσομαι ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου σου· καὶ καθὼς ὁ Πέτρος εἴρηκε· Προφήτης οὖν ὑπάρχων ὁ Δαβὶδ, καὶ εἰδὼς, ὅτι ὅρκῳ ὤμοσεν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς, ἐκ καρποῦ τῆς ὀσφύος αὐτοῦ καθίσαι τὸν Χριστὸν κατὰ σάρκα ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου αὐτοῦ· ὁτὲ δὲ ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ Υἱοῦ, ὡς ὅταν λέγῃ ὁ Ἡσαΐας· Τάδε λέγει Κύριος· Δι' ὑμᾶς διαπαντὸς τὸ ὄνομά μου βλασφημεῖται ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι.
thought_title: The Spirit shares the divine works of guiding, calling, and speaking
orientation: Marcellus continues his argument that the Holy Spirit is uncreated and equal to the Father and the Son by showing that Scripture attributes the same divine works—guiding Israel, calling apostles, and speaking through prophets—to all three persons.
pass_a_gloss: But the Holy Spirit the Scripture does not decline to call good, according to David who says: Your good Spirit will guide me in a level land. And when again the Lord says about himself: I am the living bread, the one who came down from heaven. Elsewhere he calls the Holy Spirit heavenly bread, saying: Our daily bread give us today. For he taught us in the prayer in the present age to ask for the daily bread, that is, the coming one, of which we have the firstfruits in the present life, partaking of the flesh of the Lord, just as he himself said: But the bread which I will give is my flesh for the life of the world. For the life-giving Spirit is the flesh of the Lord, because from the life-giving Spirit it was conceived. For what is born of the Spirit is Spirit. And when Jeremiah says about God, that he guided Israel in the desert: And you did not say, he says, Where is the Lord, the one who brought us up from the land of Egypt, the one who guided us in the desert? Isaiah said the Holy Spirit guided Israel in the desert; it is possible, then, to hear him saying: He led them through the deep as a horse through the desert; and they did not grow weary, and as cattle through the plain. And the Spirit came down from the Lord, and guided them. But to the Corinthians the Apostle writes, that Christ was the one guiding: For they drank from a spiritual rock that followed; and the rock was Christ. And when Paul says that he was called by God: God, he says, the one who set me apart from my mother's womb, and called me through his grace, to reveal his Son in me, so that I might preach him among the Gentiles. But he says the Romans were called by Christ, writing to them: Among whom you also are called of Jesus Christ. But the Holy Spirit, he has said, called Paul and Barnabas to preach Christ to the Gentiles. And what is indeed wonderful, when Jesus said to Paul in the temple: Go, for I am sending you far away to the Gentiles; and when Paul writes to the Galatians, Paul an apostle not from men, nor through man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father who raised him from the dead; and after a little: But I make known to you, brothers, this Gospel, that it is not according to man; for neither did I receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but through a revelation of Jesus Christ; the Holy Spirit appears to have sent both Paul and Barnabas, to preach Christ to the Gentiles. And sometimes from the person of the Father the prophets speak, as when in the Psalms God says: Once I swore in my holy one, If I lie to David, his seed will remain forever, and his throne as the sun before me; and again: From the fruit of your loins I will set upon your throne; and just as Peter has said: Therefore David, being a prophet, and knowing that God swore to him with an oath, from the fruit of his loins to seat the Christ according to the flesh upon his throne; but sometimes from the person of the Son, as when Isaiah says: Thus says the Lord: Because of you continually my name is blasphemed among the Gentiles.

choices.term: Τὸ δὲ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα οὐ παραιτεῖται ἡ Γραφὴ καλεῖν ἀγαθὸν
choices.english: But the Holy Spirit the Scripture does not decline to call good
choices.why: Keeps the Greek word order with the Holy Spirit fronted as the topic, and 'decline' preserves the sense of refusing or avoiding a title, matching the earlier contrast with the Lord declining to be called good.
rejected: But the Scripture does not refuse to call the Holy Spirit good
But the Holy Spirit the Scripture does not refuse to call good

choices.term: Τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον
choices.english: Our daily bread give us today
choices.why: Renders the petition literally with 'daily' for ἐπιούσιον, preserving the Lord's Prayer wording while keeping the imperative force.
rejected: Give us this day our daily bread
Our bread for the coming day give us today

choices.term: Πνεῦμα γὰρ ζωοποιοῦν ἡ σάρξ ἐστι τοῦ Κυρίου
choices.english: For the life-giving Spirit is the flesh of the Lord
choices.why: The Greek has Πνεῦμα as the subject and ἡ σάρξ as the predicate: 'the life-giving Spirit is the flesh of the Lord'. This preserves the theological point that the flesh of the Lord is identified with the life-giving Spirit, not the reverse.
rejected: For the flesh of the Lord is life-giving Spirit
For the flesh of the Lord is a life-giving spirit

choices.term: Ῥωμαίους δὲ ὑπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ κεκλῆσθαι λέγει
choices.english: But he says the Romans were called by Christ
choices.why: The subject of λέγει is Paul, continuing from the previous clause about Paul saying he was called by God. The pronoun 'he' refers to Paul, not to Marcellus.
rejected: But he says that the Romans were called by Christ
But the Romans, he says, were called by Christ

choices.term: ὁτὲ δὲ ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ Υἱοῦ
choices.english: but sometimes from the person of the Son
choices.why: Renders ἐκ προσώπου as 'from the person of', matching the brief's use of 'person' for the distinct reality of the divine persons, and preserves the contrast with 'from the person of the Father'.
rejected: but sometimes in the person of the Son
but sometimes on behalf of the Son

pass_b_english: But the Scripture does not decline to call the Holy Spirit good, as David says: “Your good Spirit will guide me on level ground” (Psalm 143:10). And again, when the Lord says of himself, “I am the living bread that came down from heaven” (John 6:51), elsewhere Scripture calls the Holy Spirit heavenly bread, saying, “Our daily bread give us today” (Matthew 6:11). For in the prayer he taught us to ask in this present age for the daily bread—that is, the bread of the age to come—of which we have the firstfruits in this present life by partaking of the flesh of the Lord, as he himself said: “The bread that I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world” (John 6:51). For the flesh of the Lord is life-giving spirit, because it was conceived from the life-giving Spirit. For what is born of the Spirit is spirit (John 3:6).

And when Jeremiah says about God that he guided Israel in the wilderness—“And you did not say, Where is the Lord who brought us up from the land of Egypt, who led us in the wilderness?” (Jeremiah 2:6)—Isaiah says that the Holy Spirit guided Israel in the wilderness. You can hear him say: “He led them through the deep as a horse through the wilderness, and they did not grow weary, and like cattle through the plain. And the Spirit came down from the Lord and guided them” (Isaiah 63:13-14). But to the Corinthians the apostle writes that Christ was the one guiding: “For they drank from the spiritual rock that followed, and the rock was Christ” (1 Corinthians 10:4).

And when Paul says that he was called by God—“God,” he says, “who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me by his grace, was pleased to reveal his Son in me, so that I might preach him among the Gentiles” (Galatians 1:15-16)—he says that the Romans were called by Christ, writing to them: “Among whom you also are called of Jesus Christ” (Romans 1:6). But the Holy Spirit, it says, called Paul and Barnabas to preach Christ to the Gentiles. And what is remarkable: Jesus said to Paul in the temple, “Go, for I am sending you far away to the Gentiles” (Acts 22:21), and Paul writes to the Galatians, “Paul, an apostle not from men nor through man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father who raised him from the dead” (Galatians 1:1), and a little later, “I make known to you, brothers, this gospel, that it is not according to man; for I did not receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but through a revelation of Jesus Christ” (Galatians 1:11-12). Yet the Holy Spirit is the one who appears sending Paul and Barnabas to preach Christ to the Gentiles.

And sometimes the prophets speak from the person of the Father, as when God says in the Psalms: “Once I swore in my holy one, I will not lie to David: his seed will remain forever, and his throne as the sun before me” (Psalm 89:35-36); and again: “From the fruit of your body I will set one on your throne” (Psalm 132:11). And as Peter said: “Therefore David, being a prophet and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him that from the fruit of his body he would seat the Christ on his throne according to the flesh” (Acts 2:30). But sometimes they speak from the person of the Son, as when Isaiah says: “Thus says the Lord: Because of you my name is continually blasphemed among the Gentiles” (Isaiah 52:5).

problems.quote: “I will not lie to David: his seed will remain forever, and his throne as the sun before me” (Psalm 89:35-36)
problems.source_quote: Ἅπαξ ὤμοσα ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ μου, Εἰ τῷ Δαβὶδ ψεύσομαι, τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα μενεῖ, καὶ ὁ θρόνος αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐναντίον μου
problems.why: Source has conditional Εἰ τῷ Δαβὶδ ψεύσομαι ('If I shall lie to David'), not declarative 'I will not lie to David.'
problems.fix: “Once I swore by my holiness: If I shall lie to David, his seed shall remain forever, and his throne as the sun before me” (Psalm 88:35-36)
problems.ruling: Greek has conditional εἰ...ψεύσομαι ('if I lie'); English wrongly states 'I will not lie.'

problems.quote: “Therefore David, being a prophet and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him that from the fruit of his body he would set the Christ on his throne according to the flesh” (Acts 2:30)
problems.source_quote: Προφήτης οὖν ὑπάρχων ὁ Δαβίδ, καὶ εἰδὼς, ὅτι ὅρκῳ ὤμοσεν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεός, ἐκ καρποῦ τῆς ὀσφύος αὐτοῦ καθίσαι τὸν Χριστὸν κατὰ σάρκα ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου αὐτοῦ
problems.why: Source says 'to seat the Christ on his throne according to the flesh'; English omits 'to seat' (καθίσαι) and says 'set the Christ on his throne.'
problems.fix: “…that from the fruit of his body he would seat the Christ on his throne according to the flesh” (Acts 2:30)
problems.ruling: Source has καθίσαι ('to seat'); English 'set' loses specific enthronement sense.

problems.quote: For the flesh of the Lord is life-giving Spirit
problems.source_quote: Πνεῦμα γὰρ ζωοποιοῦν ἡ σάρξ ἐστι τοῦ Κυρίου
problems.why: The Greek says 'the flesh of the Lord IS life-giving Spirit,' but the English word order 'is life-giving Spirit' could misread as 'is [the] life-giving Spirit.' The Greek has πνεῦμα as predicate nominative without article, meaning 'spirit' in quality, not the Holy Spirit. The English capitalizes 'Spirit' which risks identifying flesh as the Holy Spirit.
problems.fix: For the flesh of the Lord is life-giving spirit
problems.ruling: Πνεῦμα without article is predicate nominative; capitalizing 'Spirit' risks identifying flesh as the Holy Spirit.

last_rejected.quote: in the prayer he taught us to ask in this present age for the daily bread
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐδίδαξε γὰρ ἡμᾶς ἐν τῇ εὐχῇ ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι αἰτεῖν τὸν ἐπιούσιον ἄρτον
last_rejected.why: Misplaced modifier: 'in this present age' modifies 'to ask', not 'he taught us'. The prayer is taught for this age.
last_rejected.fix: For in the prayer he taught us, in this present age, to ask for the daily bread
last_rejected.ruling: English 'in the prayer he taught us to ask in this present age' correctly attaches 'in this present age' to 'ask,' matching ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι αἰτεῖν.

last_rejected.quote: the bread of the age to come—of which we have the firstfruits
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'of which we have the firstfruits', but English makes 'bread' the antecedent, when 'age to come' is meant.
last_rejected.fix: the bread of the age to come, of which age we have the firstfruits
last_rejected.ruling: Relative pronoun οὗ can refer to either ἄρτον or αἰῶνα; 'bread' is a valid antecedent given the Eucharistic context.

last_rejected.quote: But the Holy Spirit, it says, called Paul and Barnabas
last_rejected.source_quote: Τὸ δὲ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸν Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Βαρνάβαν κεκληκέναι εἴρηκεν
last_rejected.why: Ambiguous 'it says' hides that Scripture (Acts) is the speaker; Greek 'εἴρηκεν' has an implied subject of Scripture.
last_rejected.fix: But Scripture says that the Holy Spirit called Paul and Barnabas
last_rejected.ruling: Greek εἴρηκεν lacks explicit subject; 'it says' is acceptable. Implied Scripture subject is not mandatory to specify.

last_rejected.quote: Yet the Holy Spirit is the one who appears sending Paul and Barnabas
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἀποστεῖλαν τόν τε Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Βαρνάβαν φαίνεται
last_rejected.why: Missing subject: Greek 'φαίνεται' implies Scripture/Acts appears/shows this, not the Holy Spirit 'appears'.
last_rejected.fix: Yet Scripture shows the Holy Spirit sending Paul and Barnabas
last_rejected.ruling: φαίνεται means 'appears/clearly shows'; English 'appears sending' is awkward but not a major meaning change requiring fix.
